about: Conventions every solver follows (GR-31). CC, 2026-11-01. Tools: tools/geometry.py placed_outline; checked against shapely in graph/tests/test_model_tools.py.
units: feet and square feet; angles in degrees

lot_frame.origin: the left end of the front lot line, as seen from the street looking at the lot
lot_frame.x: along the front lot line, left to right
lot_frame.y: from the front lot line toward the rear (the lot lies at y >= 0 near the front lot line)
lot_frame.front_lot_line: lies on y = 0 for a lot whose front lot line is straight; otherwise site.front_lot_line states the segment

plan_frame.origin: the front-left corner of the plan's full outline at grade
plan_frame.x: along the plan's front face, left to right
plan_frame.y: from the front face toward the rear
plan_frame.outline: plan.footprint is the full outline at grade: walls, porches, stoops and steps included; eaves are not in it and are stated in plan.eave_ft

faces.front: the face on the plan frame's y-minimum side
faces.rear: the face on the y-maximum side
faces.left: the face on the x-minimum side
faces.right: the face on the x-maximum side

placement.names: (x, y) is where the plan frame's origin sits in the lot frame
placement.rotation: degrees counterclockwise about the plan origin, one of 0, 90, 180, 270

why: Every part of the outline, porch included, is placed by the same transform and checked against the lot outline, so a porch can never be read as off the lot or left out of a setback.
